notes.japanese: 蛮僧の治療の効は、覿面《てきめん》に現れた。
notes.problem: Unidiomatic calque; no English cure 'shows its effect on the spot'.
notes.span: The barbarian monk's cure showed its effect on the spot.
notes.suggestion: The barbarian monk's cure took effect at once.
notes.sureness: Very sure; plain idiom, no check needed.

notes.japanese: 今年で、酒虫を吐いてから、三年になるが、往年の丸丸と肥つてゐた俤《おもかげ》は、何処にもない。
notes.problem: Counting the years and naming his fatness are both literal and odd in English.
notes.span: This year is the third since he spat out the wine worm, and no trace remains of the round and sleek fullness of former years.
notes.suggestion: This is the third year since he spat out the wine worm, and no trace remains of the round, sleek fatness of former days.
notes.sureness: Sure about the idiom; less sure whether house wants 'fatness' or 'fullness' kept stable, faithful reader to confirm.

notes.japanese: 色光沢《いろつや》の悪い皮膚が、脂じみたまま、険しい顔の骨を包んで、霜に侵された双髩《さうびん》が、纔《わづか》に、顳顬《こめかみ》の上に、残つてゐるばかり、一年の中に、何度、床につくか、わからない位ださうである。
notes.problem: Dictionary English with wrong verbs: lustre does not hang, hair does not linger, no one tells time that way.
notes.span: Skin of a poor lustre hangs greasily over the bones of a gaunt face, and only a little hair, touched with frost, lingers upon his temples; they say there is no telling how many times in a year he takes to his bed.
notes.suggestion: Skin dull and greasy hangs loose over the bones of his gaunt face, and only a little frost-touched hair still clings to his temples; they say no one can count how many times a year he takes to his bed.
notes.sureness: Sure the present wording would stop a reader; wording itself could be settled by the desk against the house list for skin, hair and decline.

notes.japanese: 今では、三百畝を以て数へた負郭《ふくわく》の田も、多くは人の手に渡つた。
notes.problem: 'Suburban fields counted at' is stiff and suburban misleads; the measure reads like an inventory label.
notes.span: now of the suburban fields counted at three hundred mu, most have passed into other hands.
notes.suggestion: now most of the three hundred mu of fields around the town have passed into other hands.
notes.sureness: Sure about the English; whether to gloss mu or fukaku is for the editor, faithful reader to confirm the sense of town-edge fields.

notes.japanese: 劉自身も、余儀なく、馴れない手に鋤《すき》を執つて、佗しいその日その日を送つてゐるのである。
notes.problem: 'Willy-nilly' now means haphazard, not compelled, and no one 'passes an existence' in English.
notes.span: Liu himself has willy-nilly taken hoe in unpractised hands, and passes his wretched day-to-day existence.
notes.suggestion: Liu himself has been forced to take up the hoe with unpractised hands, and drags out his wretched day-to-day life.
notes.sureness: Very sure 'willy-nilly' and 'passes his existence' would stop a reader; 'forced' versus 'compelled' to be settled against the Japanese nuance.

notes.japanese: 現にこの疑問は、長山に住んでゐる、あらゆる職業の人人によつて繰返され、且、それらの人人の口から、あらゆる種類の答を与へられた。
notes.problem: Passive committee English with a number slip was asked, losing the narrator's light amused gossip-voice.
notes.span: In fact this question has been repeated by people of every trade living in Chozan, and answered from the mouths of those same people in every kind of way.
notes.suggestion: In fact people of every trade in Chozan have asked it again and again, and answered it themselves in every conceivable way.
notes.sureness: Sure the present rhythm sags; exact tightening is for the desk.

notes.japanese: もし酒虫を除かなかつたなら、劉は必久しからずして、死んだのに相違ない。
notes.problem: Wrong modal: 'must have died' infers a past death, it does not state the counterfactual the argument needs.
notes.span: Had the worm not been removed, Liu must before long have died, without question.
notes.suggestion: Had the worm not been removed, Liu would before long have certainly died.
notes.sureness: Very sure on the grammar; desk to match tense to house style.

notes.japanese: 劉は、昔から酒ばかり飲んでゐた。劉の一生から酒を除けば、後には、何も残らない。
notes.problem: 'From of old' is pastiche and 'remain behind' is redundant, dulling the bald equation the crux must keep bald.
notes.span: Liu from of old did nothing but drink. If wine were taken from Liu's life, nothing would remain behind.
notes.suggestion: Liu had all his life done nothing but drink. Take wine from Liu's life and nothing would remain.
notes.sureness: Sure the phrasing is unidiomatic; the desk must check the rewrite does not soften the equation into metaphor.

notes.japanese: 劉自身が既になくなつてゐたとしたら、昔日《せきじつ》の劉の健康なり家産なりが、失はれたのも、至極、当然な話であらう。
notes.problem: Hedging piles up and buries the punchline of the third answer.
notes.span: If Liu himself had already ceased to be, then it is entirely natural that the health and fortune of the Liu of former days should have been lost.
notes.suggestion: If Liu himself had already ceased to be, it is only natural that the health and fortune of the Liu of former days should be lost.
notes.sureness: Fairly sure; a straightening, not a reinterpretation, and the faithful reader should confirm nothing doctrinal is lost.

data.say: Aftermath and moral-list read literal and sagging in English and need tightening for voice without tipping the tale's refusal to choose.
